ruling.recommended_action: Refund $8.22 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the two unexempted off-route segments (RD-2 / NS-7); note the driver's breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty on the trip record; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip: total charged $55.88, made up of base $3.90, distance $39.42 on 27.96 km, time $11.07 on 42.6 min, waiting $0.02 and platform $1.47 [F8], so extra kilometres driven feed straight into the fare and RD-2's per-km branch (not the fixed-quote branch) applies [RD-2][F5].

Two off-route segments are recorded: 22:56-23:04 driving 4.61 km where the optimal route covers 2.14 km, +2.46 km, up to 871 m off route [F3]; and 23:08-23:14 driving 4.07 km where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, +3.37 km, up to 792 m off route [F4]. Those deviations (aggregate +6.5 km / +30%, +14.3 min [F1][F2]) are unexcused, so the driver did not take the shortest and most direct route [RD-1].

No exemption applies to either segment. The chat record contains no in-app messages at all [F9], so no rider message exists before 22:56:55 or before 23:08:05 to found an agreement; the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a statement, not rider consent, and appears only in his own words [F10], so it cannot exempt a segment [RD-5]. The chat record is complete (empty, not a hole), so the RD-5 finding is that the segment counts, not undetermined. On RD-3, the trace measures no stop inside either segment and no rider message names a place [F3][F4][F9], so no rider-requested-stop exemption arises [RD-3]. On RD-4, no incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F13], and the only speed records, East Coast Parkway band 4 at 30-39 km/h [F11] and Airport Boulevard band 4 [F12], are neither incidents under RD-4(a) nor the band 1/2 congestion that RD-4(b) requires to stand alone; the weather was fair [F14], so neither segment is exempted [RD-4].

Amount: the trip's per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare divided by distance km = $39.42 / 27.96 km = $1.4099/km [F5][F8]. Unexempted segment kilometres = 2.46 km [F3] + 3.37 km [F4] = 5.83 km; 5.83 km x $1.4099/km = $8.2197, which rounds to $8.22 [RD-2]. The residual about 0.66 km between the 6.49 km billed as excess [F5] and the 5.83 km inside the recorded segments (corridor and matching mileage not attributed to any segment) is not refundable under RD-2 [RD-2]. The $0.02 waiting unit [F6] and the 1.0x surge factor [F7] are untouched, and no ERP or toll overcharge is in issue [RD-3]. The driver has zero upheld disputes, including zero route disputes, in the last 90 days [F16], so the repeated-breach condition of RD-6 is not met and no account flag attaches; profile facts are not used to establish liability on either side [F15][F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the empty chat record [F9] and the driver's statement [F10]; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexually suggestive or alleging dangerous driving. The statement is a bare denial about fare and GPS. No safety basis, no escalation.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 22:56-23:04 adds 2.46 km, up to 871 m off the optimal route [F3]. The complete, empty chat record means no rider message exists before the segment start [F9]; the driver's post-trip statement about GPS rerouting is a statement, not rider consent, and appears only in his own words [F10], so upon RD-5 it gives no exemption [RD-5]. No stop is measured in the segment and no rider message names a place [F3][F9], so RD-3 gives no exemption [RD-3]. No incident on the route in the window [F13] and only band 4 speeds [F11][F12], so RD-4 gives no exemption [RD-4]. The 2.46 km is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

Off-route segment 23:08-23:14 adds 3.37 km, up to 792 m off the optimal route [F4]. The empty chat record [F9] means no rider agreement precedes the segment start, and the driver's post-trip statement cannot serve as consent [F10][RD-5]. No rider-requested stop is measured or named [F4][F9][RD-3], and neither the absent incidents [F13] nor the band 4 speed records [F11][F12] exempt it [RD-4]. The 3.37 km is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as to the RD-1 breach (aggregate +6.5 km / +30% [F1], +14.3 min [F2]) but not as a measure of refund: RD-2 refunds only the kilometres inside the recorded off-route segments [F3][F4], so the aggregate cannot enlarge the amount [RD-2].

The request for account review is rejected: the driver has route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so the repeated condition of RD-6 is not met and no flag_account attaches [RD-6]; liability rests on the segments [F3][F4] alone.
The driver's mitigation fails: band 4 at 30-39 km/h [F11][F12] is neither an incident under RD-4(a) nor band 1/2 congestion, and under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own [RD-4].

The driver's conclusion that no flag attaches is accepted (0 upheld route disputes [F16], RD-6 not met), but that does not reduce the refund exposure, which flows from RD-2 on the segment kilometres [F3][F4], not from RD-6 [RD-2].
Accepted that no profile fact decides liability: the rider's 0 upheld disputes [F15] is background only and cannot offset the driver's established RD-1 breach [RD-1].
The driver's point that only 5.83 km of the 6.5 km excess is recoverable is accepted [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]; the residual about 0.66 km of the 6.49 km billed [F5] is not refundable [RD-2].
